slides.0.title: Grapes and styles
slides.0.subtitle: Red dominates, and vin gris is the most distinctive style
slides.1.title: Red grapes: two generations
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The traditional base
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Cinsault leads, at nearly 40% in 2005, followed by Carignan, Alicante Bouschet and Grenache: heat-tolerant, productive southern French grapes
slides.1.highlights.1.title: International grapes
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah drove the revival and appear in many top wines
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The permitted list
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The AOG list has 15 red and rosé grapes, including Tempranillo, Mourvèdre, Tannat, Cot (Malbec), Petit Verdot, Cabernet Franc, Gamay and Pinot
slides.1.content: Think tradition with Cinsault and Carignan, modern premium with Syrah and Cabernet.
slides.2.title: White grapes and local names
slides.2.highlights.0.title: A small share
slides.2.highlights.0.content: White wine was only about 3% of output in 2005. Traditional white grapes include Clairette and Muscat
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The permitted list
slides.2.highlights.1.content: It also includes Chardonnay, Sauvignon, Ugni Blanc, Grenache Blanc, Macabeo and Pedro Ximénez, among others
slides.2.highlights.2.title: A local name
slides.2.highlights.2.content: El Biod, also called Zerhouni, echoes the name Zerhoun and is one of the few local names in the regulation
slides.2.content: White wine is not the mainstream, but the list reveals links with France and Spain.
slides.3.title: Vin gris and rosé
slides.3.highlights.0.title: A significant share
slides.3.highlights.0.content: In 2005 red exceeded 75%, with rosé and vin gris together about 20%, far ahead of white
slides.3.highlights.1.title: A recognised category
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The rules of Coteaux de l'Atlas and Les Côtes de Rommani list red, rosé, gris and white side by side, with one set of sugar and alcohol minimums for rosé and gris
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Doukkala
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The only one of the 14 AOGs limited to rosé, made solely from the local "gros rosé des Doukkala" clones
slides.3.content: Remember vin gris's legal standing: in Morocco it is a category written into the rules.
slides.4.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge check
Which grape was most planted in Morocco in 2005?
Nearly 40%, ahead of Carignan, which once led.
Which is closest to the 2005 production mix?
A. Rosé over 75%, red about 20%, white about 3%
B. Red over 75%, rosé and gris about 20%, white about 3%
C. White over 75%, red about 20%, rosé about 3%
Red dominates and white is a small share.
Which AOG is legally limited to rosé?
And only from the "gros rosé des Doukkala" clones.
